summary: As of October 28, 2026, junk-bond spreads are 3.14 percentage points, -0.13 percentage points over five trading days, and the junk-versus-safe gap is 2.28 percentage points. VIX is 16.91 and the 3-month VIX is 19.22, so near-term fear is below the 3-month reading. The Nasdaq-100 is -4.5 percent from its trailing high, semiconductors are +9.6 percent versus their 200-day average, and 73 percent of the 30-name list is above its own 200-day average.
what_would_change_this: The headline would leave risk-on if junk spreads reached 4.50 percentage points, near-term volatility rose above the 3-month reading by more than half a point, or the Nasdaq-100 fell more than 10 percent below its trailing high.
what_the_tape_is_saying: As of October 28, 2026, junk-bond spreads are 3.14 percentage points and are down 0.13 percentage points over five trading days. Investment-grade spreads are down 0.02 percentage points over those same five trading days. The CCC-minus-BB gap is 11.23 percentage points. Of the 0.23 percentage-point move in the all-in junk yield, 0.13 was the credit spread and 0.10 was Treasury rates. The 10-year yield is 4.99 percent as of October 27, 2026 and the 30-year is 5.30 percent as of October 27, 2026, a gap of 0.31 percentage points. Brent is 110.44 dollars a barrel as of October 28, 2026 (+1.49 percent over five trading days), and the curve is an unpublished curve shape. The 5-year inflation breakeven is 2.49 percent as of October 28, 2026, up 0.09 percentage points over five observations. The 10-year real yield is 2.64 percent as of October 27, 2026. The broad dollar index is 121.32 as of October 23, 2026, +0.77 index points over 20 observations. VIX is 16.91 as of October 28, 2026. The Fed balance sheet is 6.75 trillion dollars as of October 21, 2026, up 6 billion dollars over the latest four weekly observations.
